title: After flight delay, Donovan Mitchell wanted game postponed. The Cavs bench stepped up instead
content:
Donovan Mitchell didn’t even want his Cleveland Cavaliers to play Saturday against the Dallas Mavericks.

The Cavaliers got stuck in Miami on Friday after the Federal Aviation Administration grounded all domestic flights for over four hours earlier that night, and they couldn’t make the trip home to play the second game of their back-to-back until Saturday morning.

Mitchell didn’t see the extraordinary conditions, lack of rest and condensed travel time as a fair set of circumstances.

Asked if he would prefer to see the game postponed, he responded, “Yeah, sure.”

“This is unprecedented,” Mitchell told reporters, according to Cleveland.com’s Chris Fedor. “Back-to-back. Three-hour flight. It was already going to be a tough one. But if they say we have to play, then we have to play.”

Mitchell didn’t play.

Neither did any of the Cavaliers’ (7-7) starting five. Evan Mobley sat for a second straight game with a left big toe sprain, while the other four rested.

Cleveland beat the Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving-led Mavericks 127-117 without them.

“You know, that’s a special win,” Atkinson said post game “Just all the circumstances, everything around it. … Says a lot about our young guys, really. We’ve been talking about it since day one in training camp — these guys are impressing.

“…We shouldn’t be surprised, they’ve been great since the first day of training camp, so it’s great to confirm that.”

Cavs coach Kenny Atkinson decided to rest his stars and told reporters pregame that the team would “have to deal with different circumstances, obviously, in this case, but we’ll go out and compete and make the fans proud of us.”

With Mitchell, James Harden, Peyton Watson, Jarrett Allen and Mobley unavailable, the Cavaliers’ second unit started and finished Dallas off, showcasing the Eastern Conference runner-up’s depth.

Cleveland rolled out a starting five of forward Jaylon Tyson (18 points), guard Tyrese Proctor (24 points), guard Meleek Thomas (20 points), and two first-time Cleveland starters this season in center Thomas Bryant (19 points) and wing Mario Hezonja (22 points). The Cavaliers also got double-digit scoring off the bench from Norchad Omier, who played a season-high 27 minutes.

Proctor tallied a triple-double with 11 rebounds and 10 assists, while Bryant contributed 11 boards.

“Give our front office credit. They find guys,” Atkinson said postgame. “They bring in guys here, I like them all.”

The second unit proved enough to outmatch Dallas and its stars. All told, Cleveland shot 53 percent from the field, 38 percent from deep and 89 percent from the free-throw line, with 54 rebounds and 31 assists. Nearly every team metric was better than Dallas’ on Saturday.

Irving scored 34 in the losing effort while Flagg added 18 points, eight rebounds and five assists.

Atkinson maintained pregame that the circumstances could’ve been more dire.

“It could have been a lot worse,” he said. “We got lucky to get back into a hotel after the game because it was really busy in Miami. And we’re lucky we got out and got in here early today.”
